rows.description: A teenager talks up money, girlfriends or fights so the group will rank them higher. Others may roll their eyes or quietly distance themselves, which the boaster rarely notices.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A person who is secure lets results speak, shares wins simply, and asks about others. Needing no applause is the sign that the achievement is truly their own.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A colleague sees a peer keep listing achievements and reads it as a hunger for reassurance more than arrogance. Kind, specific acknowledgement often lowers the need to brag.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A teenager who lost a friendship insists the other person was the only problem. The story eases guilt, but it also blocks the learning that could repair the next friendship.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A student skips study for weeks and tells themselves they work better under pressure. The story protects self-image from the discomfort of the real reason, which is often fear of failing.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: An adult in a bad job, relationship or debt pattern keeps saying it will sort itself out. Looking straight at it would demand action they are not ready for, so the mind averts its gaze.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A person asks what they would say if a friend told them this same story, or what evidence would change their mind. Self-honesty grows through kind, steady questions, not harsh self-attack.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A small child promises to share, clean up or not cry and means it fully in that moment. They do not yet grasp that a promise binds a later self who will feel differently.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A schoolchild who promised a friend to keep a secret or come to the game feels real discomfort when it gets hard. Keeping the word through inconvenience builds a reputation and an inner sense of being reliable.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Being let down by a broken promise [Receiver]
rows.description: A teenager whose parent forgets a promised event stores it as proof that they are not a priority. Repeated small breakages teach people to stop hoping and to stop asking.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
